claims.text: Stepwise thermo-mechanical processing using controlled heating, deformation, and cooling cycles will generate dual coherent precipitates in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Generating dual coherent precipitates through stepwise thermo-mechanical processing will improve the strength-plasticity balance relative to conventional processing.
The initial refractory high-entropy alloy has a relatively uniform matrix.
The initial alloy contains no intentionally introduced coherent precipitates.
The alloy must contain precipitate-forming elements for the intervention to work.
Controlled processing conditions can facilitate coherent precipitate formation.
The processing temperature, strain, and cooling rate must be optimized for the alloy composition.
Dual coherent precipitates block dislocation motion.
Blocking dislocation motion with dual coherent precipitates enhances work hardening.
Dual coherent precipitates increase yield strength.
Dual coherent precipitates maintain or improve ductility through localized deformation mechanisms.
The proposed processing will produce higher yield strength than conventional thermo-mechanical processing.
The proposed processing will sustain or improve ductility relative to conventional thermo-mechanical processing.
Alloys lacking a composition suitable for coherent precipitate formation may not exhibit improved properties.
Suboptimal processing conditions may prevent the predicted property improvement.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement depends on alloy composition and control of processing parameters.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant yield-strength increase while maintaining or improving ductility is designated as a falsifying result.
Failure to confirm dual coherent precipitates by TEM is designated as a falsifying result.
